expectations.text: States that instructions to a model are not enforcement, regardless of wording or emphasis
expectations.evidence: Caps and repetition don't fix this; they just make the training stronger, not the device

expectations.text: Redirects away from rewording CLAUDE.md as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: Then remove those rules from CLAUDE.md—or reframe them as 'why these devices exist' rather than 'do this or else.'

expectations.text: Recommends permission deny rules in settings.json with concrete syntax
expectations.evidence: Recommends git hooks in .git/hooks/, not settings.json

expectations.text: Recommends a PreToolUse hook for cases that need logic rather than a pattern match
expectations.evidence: Recommends shell-based git hooks (pre-commit, pre-push), not Claude Code PreToolUse hooks

expectations.text: Explains that the deny message should say what to do instead, not merely refuse
expectations.evidence: Messages are only refusals: 'ERROR: Do not edit files...' and 'ERROR: Force push is forbidden' with no guidance on alternatives

expectations.text: Recommends verifying the device actually fires rather than assuming it works
expectations.evidence: No mention of testing or verifying hooks work

expectations.text: Recommends committing the rules so they apply to the whole team, not just one machine
expectations.evidence: Standard .git/hooks placement is local to the machine; no mention of version control or team application

expectations.text: Explains why repetition and capitals do not make an instruction reliable
expectations.evidence: Instructions are...compressed out of the active context window as your conversation lengthens...Caps and repetition don't fix this
